  "title": "The Treasury is watching",
  "type": "macro",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-08-20",
  "insights": [
   "The US Treasury announced a doubling of long-end buyback operations in the 10-20y and 20-30y sectors, starting September 9, 2026.",
   "The move effectively reduces long-end duration supply by approximately $100bn in 10y-equivalent terms annually, signaling the Treasury's sensitivity to rising long-term yields.",
   "Buyback sizes will increase from a maximum of $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, with the additional purchases financed through increased bill issuance rather than changes to coupon auction sizes.",
   "Barclays estimates the announcement could lower the long-end term premium by roughly 10bp, assuming the market views the reduction as a permanent decrease in budget deficits.",
   "The Treasury maintains the option to further increase buybacks or modify auction guidance at the November meeting if the recent rally in long-end yields reverses.",
   "Japan's experience with issuance cuts since 2025 serves as a warning that such measures often provide only temporary relief, with fiscal consolidation remaining the primary driver for long-term yield pressure."
